name: IN-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Prediction markets price a Republican win near 96%
model.rationale: An R+16 district, an incumbent with a roughly 65-to-1 fundraising advantage, and markets pricing the Republican near 96% all point the same way, and no polling or expert ratings suggest competition.
model.watch: A heavy Democratic wave environment or a late scandal involving Shreve could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would require far more than current evidence shows.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 6th District sits firmly in Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly sixteen points toward the GOP. Republican incumbent Jefferson Shreve is running for re-election and holds every visible advantage. He has raised about $2.4 million and reports $1.6 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Cinde Wirth has raised roughly $37,000 with about $7,000 available. No independent polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give the Republican about a 96% chance of winning.

The forecast expects Shreve to win by a wide, double-digit margin. Even if the national climate in 2026 favors Democrats, the district's deep Republican lean and the incumbent's financial dominance make a competitive race unlikely. The Democratic path would require an unusually large wave combined with resources the challenger has not demonstrated.
